data.one_liner: Renders declarative widget description files at runtime for Remote Flutter Widgets.
data.what_it_does: Allows Flutter apps to render remote widget descriptions obtained dynamically at runtime. It combines a runtime engine, configuration data, and local widget libraries to build arbitrary widget trees.
use_when: You need to display dynamic UI or search results that could not be known when the app was created.
You want to build database frontends with bespoke UIs for editing different types of objects.
avoid_when: You want to create completely new custom widgets involving page transitions, drag and drop, or custom painters.
You want to update the core application look, feel, or navigation which should be shipped via normal updates.
strengths: Keeps formats and supported widget sets backwards compatible.
Supports both text and binary formats for transporting remote widget libraries and data.
Can be used on the server or command-line for parts dealing only with formats.
weaknesses: Cannot create complex custom widgets or custom painters from the remote descriptions.
Potential theoretical performance limitations depending on implementation scale.
data.setup_notes: No special native permissions or build_runner steps required; simply include the package and initialize Runtime and DynamicContent.
